reason: A high-confidence independent reproducer violates coordinated DOM transition atomicity. Full matrix reruns were deliberately stopped before execution, as required by the acceptance stop condition.

findings.title: Rejected coordinated DOM group leaves an earlier member running
reproduction: Open /integration.html?dom on the retained development server.
Add #replacement { transform-origin: 50% 50% !important; } to an authored stylesheet.
Call integrationProbe.group with stage and replacement, both using identity-to-x30 keyframes and duration 800ms.
The call throws Declarative DOM presentation was overridden by authored CSS.
Immediately afterward stage remains registered as an active declarative motion and has new owned inline presentation declarations.
After 150ms stage has advanced to x=5.617500000447035 despite the group call having failed.
findings.cause: The preparation helper only checks important transform/opacity and individual transforms. Actual transform-origin precedence is checked during beginTransition.apply(0). Group members are begun with sequential map and have no transaction rollback when a later begin throws.
findings.impact: The caller receives no returned handles while a prior group member has already mutated and continues animating. This violates the documented all-or-nothing preparation contract, not merely a diagnostic wording expectation.
findings.requiredCorrection: Make all potentially failing DOM preparation transactional before starting or replacing any member, or restore every member and preserve prior handles/state when a start fails. Include a focused regression for important transform-origin on a later member and retain existing invalid-group and replacement behavior.
